bill_title: Regulatory Accountability Act of 2015
aflcio_description: This bill would tilt the regulatory process further in favor of business groups and those who want to stop regulations, and make it much more difficult for the government to protect workers and the public. The bill adds dozens of new analytical and procedural requirements to the rulemaking process, which adds years to the process. It upends more than 40 years of labor, health, safety and environmental laws and threaten new needed protections. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act Repeal
aflcio_description: This bill would repeal the Affordable Care Act which provides insurance coverage to millions of Americans who otherwise would be uninsured. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act of 2015
aflcio_description: This bill would add burdensome and costly analytical and procedural requirements to the rulemaking process making it much more difficult to issue needed protections. The development of major workplace safety rules already takes 6-10 years; this bill would further delay these rules and more workers would pay with their lives. This legislation makes costs and impacts on businesses the primary consideration in establishing new rules, instead of protecting the public. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Amendment to Defund Amtrak
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Tom McClintock (R-Calif.) to the Passenger Rail Reform and Investment Act of 2015 (H.R. 749) would zero out federal funding for our national passenger rail carrier. Every mode of transportation needs some type of federal support to survive and operate efficiently and passenger rail is no different. Amtrak has made significant improvements to its service and is now an important driver of jobs and economic development. The McClintock amendment would gut our nation's passenger rail network, completely undercutting the important work the transportation bill accomplishes. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Resolution Overturning the NLRB's Updated Election Procedures
aflcio_description: The National Labor Relations Board modernized its election procedures to reduce unnecessary litigation and delay in the election process. The moderinzed rules, issued on December 12, 2014, make the election process run more smoothly and predictably, to the benefit of employers, workers and unions. This resolution of disapproval is extreme and would roll back and undermine workers' rights to a fair and timely election process on union representation. The resolution passed the Senate and House, but vetoed by President Obama.

bill_title: FY2016 Budget Resolution
aflcio_description: This reckless budget resolution introduced by Rep. Tom Price (R-Ga.) favors large corporations and the wealthy while slashing programs that serve moderate and low-income families. Rather than investing in the middle class, this budget would cut more than $5 trillion in programs that help working families, including education, workforce training, public health, research, infrastructure and other critical investments. According to the Center for Budget and Policy Priorities, 69% of these budget cuts would come from programs that serve people with low incomes, including health assistance, food programs and student loans. Overall, the budget would cut non-defense discretionary programs nearly 40% below the lowest level in the last 50 years. The resolution was agreed to in the House.

bill_title: Amendment to Limit Federal Employees' Collective Bargaining Rights
aflcio_description: This amendment by Jody B. Hice (R-Ga.) to the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016 (H.R. 2029) would bar the use of funds provided by the bill to pay a federal employee during any period when that employee is using "official time" to represent a union or its bargaining unit employees. This amendment serves no purpose but to erode collective bargaining rights for civil service federal employees, and at greater cost to American taxpayers. Union representation for employees working their way through administrative procedures is a cost-effective process for administrating and adjudicating agency policies. The alternative to official time is for government agencies to pay for costly third-party attorney and arbitrator fees. Using this time for internal union business is strictly prohibited by law: official time may not be used to solicit membership, conduct internal union meetings, elect union officers or engage in partisan political activities. The notion that official time is used for these purposes is blatantly false. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Prevailing Wage Laws
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Steve King (R-Iowa) to the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2016 (H.R. 2029) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015
aflcio_description: This bill emerged from the Senate with bipartisan support and included enforcement provisions supported by both labor and industry, but was subsequently loaded by House Republican leadership with numerous controversial and partisan provisions that weaken, or unacceptably alter it, and make it more difficult to negotiate agreements that are good for workers and the environment. Stripped from the customs bill is a currency provision the administration opposes. This bipartisan provision, supported by labor and business, was potentially the most critical enforcement tool in the entire package. It would have allowed the U.S. to treat currency manipulation as a countervailable subsidy. Also added to the customs bill was unacceptable language weakening the "Menendez Amendment," which requires countries to thoroughly address human trafficking before they could be included in a fast-tracked trade deal with the United States. The bill passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Obama and became law on February 24, 2016.

bill_title: Defending Public Safety Employees' Retirement Act
aflcio_description: This bill includes trade-related provisions to grant authority to the president to "fast track" trade agreements. It fails to hold the executive branch accountable to acheive negotiating objectives, address the job-killing U.S. trade imbalance, which currently stands at $505 billion, or ensures that trade deals do not continue the current race to the bottom in terms of pay and benefits, worker rights, environmental protections, access to affordable medicines, food safety rules and other vital protections for working families. In short, it does nothing to prevent the mistakes of the failed trade policies that have contributed to stagnating wages, increasing inequality and the closure of more than 60,000 factories since 2000. The bill passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Obama and became law on June 29, 2015.

bill_title: Enforce the Law for Sanctuary Cities Act
aflcio_description: This bill penalizes local law enforcement agencies for insisting on due process protections for immigrant community members and instituting policies that prioritize community safety, must be rejected. The AFL-CIO strongly supports comprehensive immigration reform and knows that creating a broad and inclusive pathway to citizenship uplifts workers' rights, boosts our economy, and makes our communities both safer and more just. By contrast, the piecemeal, enforcement-only approaches found in this bill only further entrench fear and mistrust in our communities. These practices also lend credence to a corrosive, anti-immigrant narrative. The bill passed the House.

bill_title: REINS Act of 2015
aflcio_description: The Regulations from the Executive in Need of Scrutiny (REINS) Act of 2015 (H.R. 427) would cripple a regulatory process that already causes excessive delays in the issuance of crucial worker and public protections. It would radically alter the regulatory process by requiring Congress to vote to approve all major rules before they can go into effect. This is an extreme measure that would make it virtually impossible for agencies to issue any meaningful rules, threatening the health and safety of workers and the public. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Amendment to Protect Due Process
aflcio_description: This substitute amendment by Rep. Mark Takano (D-Calif.) to the VA Accountability Act of 2015 (H.R. 1994) would establish improved employee accountability measures while protecting the basic due process rights of the front-line workforce. The substitute amendment includes an exception to current civil service protections where an employee presents a direct threat to public health, but would retain post-removal appeal rights, including notice, a hearing and a written decision. The amendment failed.

bill_title: VA Accountability Act of 2015
aflcio_description: This bill eliminates fundamental due process rights for non-management Veterans Affairs employees, including more than 100,000 veterans in the VA workforce. These employees would become "at-will" and subject to the whims of managers and face discrimination, retaliation and patronage without recourse or due process. This bill does nothing to increase accountability but diminishes the VA's ability to recruit and retain a top-notch workforce. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Amendment to Strike the Maritime Security Program Provision
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Justin Amash (R-Mich.) would strike the Maritime Security Program (MSP) provision, the lifeblood of a commercial fleet of private and militarily-useful vessels, employing highly trained U.S. mariners who heed the call of the U.S. military wherever needed. The MSP fleet represents one of the most efficient investments of taxpayer dollars. Striking the MSP provision will damage our national security, our military's ability to project power overseas and would force thousands of middle-class mariners out of work. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Scholarships for Opportunity and Results (SOAR) Reauthorization Act
aflcio_description: This bill would reauthorize the District of Columbia private school voucher program, though evidence repeatedly has shown vouchers fail to achieve their intended purpose of improving student outcomes. American public schools, unlike private schools, are open and nondiscriminatory; they accept all students. Private schools can pick and choose which students to accept and may turn away students or families with greater needs. Vouchers redirect funding away from the public schools, leaving them with fewer resources to serve all children. Especially in this era of sequester-imposed spending caps where every dollar matters, public funds must be directed to public schools to make them stronger, not spent on private schools. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Retail Investor Protection Act
aflcio_description: This misnamed bill would derail the Department of Labor from moving forward with its long-overdue and important rulemaking to protect retirement investors from financial advisors' harmful conflicts of interest. The American public loses an estimated $17 billion per year as a result of retirement investment advice that is not in their best interest. This bill blocks the rulemaking until the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has finalized its new rules concerning the duties of brokers to their customers. It also prevents the SEC from acting until it complies with new reporting and analysis requirements that provide no meaningful benefit to investors, but delays regulatory action. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Export-Import Bank Reform and Reauthorization Act
aflcio_description: The Export-Import Bank is a vital institution with a decades-long track record of success in supporting United States exports, jobs and economic competitiveness. In a highly-globalized economy filled with foreign firms striving to capture market share held by U.S. firms, often with the assistance of targeted public polices, and often acting through state-owned or state-supported enterprises, the Export-Import Bank helps level the international playing field. Maintaining and increasing exports of American manufactured products, agricultural goods and services is a key growth strategy for the U.S. economy. Failing to reauthorize the Bank would do irreparable harm to the U.S. economy and would jeopardize the economic future of thousands of American families. The Export-Import Bank is the only trade-focused government agency whose mandate includes U.S. job creation. The reauthorization passed.

bill_title: Amendment to Repeal Prevailing Wage Laws
aflcio_description: This amendment by Rep. Steve King (R-Iowa) to the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act (H.R. 22) would have repealed Davis-Bacon coverage for projects funded under this bill. The Davis-Bacon Act requires companies to pay construction workers locally prevailing wages on federally funded projects. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Amendment to Defund the Export-Import Bank
aflcio_description: The Export-Import Bank helps create and maintain thousands of jobs in the United States by financing the export of U.S. goods and services. A number of amendments were offered to weaken or eliminate the Export-Import bank and the jobs it supports. This amendment by Rep. Scott Perry (R-Pa.) to the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act (H.R. 22) would limit the percentage of funding available for loans to large exporters. The amendment failed.

bill_title: Tribal Labor Sovereignty Act of 2015
aflcio_description: This bill strips National Labor Relations Act protections from more than 700,000 workers at tribal enterprises on tribal lands. It denies workers legally enforceable rights to form unions and bargain collectively in instances where they are working for a tribal enterprise, which is simply a commercial operation competing with non-tribal businesses. The vast majority of employees of these commercial enterprises, such as casinos, are not Native Americans. This legislation leaves workers with no voice in setting tribal policy and no recourse to tribal governments for the protection of their rights. The bill passed the House amended.

bill_title: Motion to Strengthen Currency Manipulation Provisions
corrections: vote_question passage -> motion: Voteview roll 652 of the 114th is 'On Motion to Instruct Conferees' on H.R. 644, which failed 193-232. The record's own description says so - 'This motion instructed conferees to include the stronger... currency manipulation provisions' - and a motion to instruct does not dispose of the bill
aflcio_description: This motion instructed conferees to include the stronger, enforceable currency manipulation provisions contained in the Senate Customs bill. Unfortunately, the motion failed and the House stripped from the final bill the currency provision that would have made clear the U.S. can treat currency manipulation as a countervailable subsidy. The remaining currency provisions simply call for "engagement" and reference so-called "consequences," which simply won't work.

bill_title: Fixing America's Surface Transportation (FAST) Act
corrections: vote_question 'passage' -> 'conference report': the roll call's own question is 'On Agreeing to the Conference Report'. The scorecard's value was inferred from its prose, which the 11 Aug 2026 review measured at ~8% wrong; result 'Passed' -> 'Adopted', which follows the roll call ('Passed') and the collection's convention for a conference report
aflcio_description: This bipartisan, long-term funding bill for our nation's transit systems, highways, bridges and passenger rail networks breaks the cycle of flat-line funding and short-term extensions that has strangled our economy and stunted job creation. The FAST Act strikes the right balance on many important policy issues that were considered, including measures to address bus driver assaults, responsible transit public-private partnerships, improved Buy America rules, rail safety and the transport of hazardous materials. The bill includes the reauthorization of the Export-Import Bank, which will help American manufacturers and their employees compete with foreign companies and support good middle-class jobs in this country. The bill passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Obama and became law on December 4, 2015.

aflcio_description: The conference report on the Customs Bill was loaded up with numerous controversial and partisan provisions that weakened, or unacceptably altered it, and would make it more difficult to negotiate trade agreements that are good for workers. Stripped from the final bill was a critical bipartisan currency provision that would have made clear the U.S. can treat currency manipulation as a countervailable subsidy. The bill also contained harmful language that U.S. free trade agreements must not include obligations regarding greenhouse gas emissions. Slipped in at the last minute was the harmful and unrelated Permanent Internet Tax Freedom Act, which bans the authority of state and local governments to impose taxes on internet access, restricting the ability of state and local governments to raise funds to invest in needed infrastructure, education, health care, job training and other vital public services. The bill passed the House and Senate, was signed by President Obama and became law on February 24, 2016.
